items.title: Driekwart Nederlanders wil zelf bepalen welke informatie zij online te zien krijgen
items.raw_text: Driekwart van de Nederlanders (75%) wil zelf bepalen van welke bronnen zij nieuws te zien krijgen, in plaats van dat een algoritme die keuze maakt. Daarbij maakt 73% zich zorgen over de betrouwbaarheid van informatie. Ook wil 70% informatie kunnen zoeken zonder dat eerder zoek- en klikgedrag bepaalt welke resultaten verschijnen. Tegelijkertijd zegt ruim een derde (34%) de zoektocht naar informatie steeds vaker bij AI-toepassingen zoals ChatGPT te beginnen. Dat staat in een nieuw, jaarlijks onderzoek van KB nationale bibliotheek , uitgevoerd door Motivaction. (Download onder dit artikel) De KB wil met dit onderzoek de ontwikkelingen in het informatiezoekgedrag van Nederlanders in kaart brengen. Als nationale bibliotheek beschouwt de KB vrije toegang tot oorspronkelijke informatie en het zelfstandig kunnen raadplegen van bronnen als een democratisch recht. items.title: The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel
items.raw_text: Avi Davidson lost his left hand as a teenager. Since then, he’s cycled through a few prosthetics. But his latest is different—it’s wired up to nerves in the upper part of his forearm and allows him to feel pressure. For the first time in years, he can use his left limb to handle delicate objects like grapes, eggs, and a loved one’s hand. Davidson, who is taking part in a clinical trial run by the University of Utah, is the ninth person to have this experimental device implanted in his arm. But he’s the first to take it home and use it independently. The hand is part of the bionic LUKE arm, named after Luke Skywalker of Star Wars , who was fitted with a lifelike prosthetic arm after his own was light-sabered off . The arm was developed in the 2000s , initially trialed in 2014 , and approved by the FDA that same year. The trial that Davidson is enrolled in isn’t so focused on the arm itself but on a new way to connect it to a person’s nervous system. The connection allows users to control movements and receive feedback about how much pressure they’re applying. Researchers hope that Davidson’s experiences will help them answer some long-standing questions about the technology, including how useful it really is in day-to-day life. They want to know when the device is helpful and where it might fail. They also want to learn how it might affect Davidson’s well-being as well as his brain and nervous system. items.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
items.raw_text: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025 . It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics. Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO . In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk you are plain out of luck. sqlite3_rsync can copy a snapshot of your database over an SSH connection to another machine, without first needing to create a full local copy! It's also good for synchronizing an existing copy of a database without re-transmitting the entire thing over the network. It works in a similar way to regular rsync: The core idea behind the protocol is that the replica sends cryptographic hashes for pages or groups of pages over to the origin side. The origin sends back page content that differs, or requests finer-grain hashes if a multi-page hash does not match. If the origin and replica start out being vastly different, the total network bandwidth can exceed the size of the entire database, due to the overhead of exchanging hashes, but the excess bandwidth is not great - a few percent at most. items.title: How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
items.raw_text: In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote a feature story describing how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I’ve lost count of how many times he’s already been proved right. Sure, it’s technically possible to meet the world’s rising electricity demand with other power sources, including renewables like wind and solar supported by batteries. But the reality in the US so far is that the data center boom is helping to fuel a massive natural-gas resurgence. Just one example: Plans for the Meta data center in Louisiana that David focused on in his story have expanded, and its power needs have too. The local utility went from three planned natural-gas plants to 10 . And as I wrote in a new story this week, data center developers are now looking beyond the grid and planning to build their own off-grid gas power plants . How did we get here? If you want to understand the future of the grid, one way to do it is by looking at interconnection queues—lists of power plants that have requested a connection to the system. In recent years these queues have been dominated by renewables like wind and solar power, which are generally the cheapest way to build new energy capacity today. But there’s been a shift in some places, particularly for PJM, the country’s largest power grid operator, which covers parts of 13 states in an area stretching from Illinois to Washington, DC. items.title: Rapportagetags: zo win je tijd bij de Wsob-rapportage
items.raw_text: Gebruik jij net als veel bibliotheken Olifantenpaadje om je activiteiten te beheren? Van workshops en lezingen tot cursussen en leesclubs: het systeem brengt aanbod, planning en inschrijvingen samen op één plek. Ook voor de jaarlijkse Wsob-rapportage is Olifantenpaadje een handig hulpmiddel. Maar hoe filter je eenvoudig op de vijf wettelijke kernfuncties van jouw bibliotheek? Daarvoor bedachten Marlon van der Zwaan en Jochem Bootsma van BIJ de bieb een praktische oplossing. Een kleine aanpassing, meer inzicht ‘Wij wilden kunnen rapporteren en uitfilteren op activiteiten binnen de vijf kernfuncties’, zeggen zij. ‘Maar in Olifantenpaadje is het niet verplicht op bij ieder nieuw product een van deze kernfuncties in te voeren’. De oplossing? Bij de Bieb voegde rapportagetags toe aan Olifantenpaadje, één voor elke kernfunctie. Ook kwam er een extra tag voor community-activiteiten. Deze tags verschijnen als eerste wanneer iemand tags aan een activiteit toevoegen. Alle andere tags zijn algemene tags of organisatortags geworden. Zo kunnen medewerkers activiteiten op een eenduidige manier registreren. En kan BIJ de bieb de gegevens gerichter filteren, voor beter inzicht in de activiteiten. Trainingen in alle teams Om iedereen met de nieuwe werkwijze te laten werken, organiseerden Marlon en Jochem trainingen in alle teams. Ook kregen de coördinatoren uitleg over de rapportages en rapportagetags. Zij helpen hun teams om activiteiten op de juiste manier in Olifantenpaadje vast te leggen.

items.raw_text: De Consumentenbond en de stichtingen Offlimits en The Firewall willen dat de camerabril van Meta verboden wordt. De drie organisaties pleitten daar vandaag voor in de rechtbank in Amsterdam. Meta, ook het bedrijf achter Facebook, Instagram en WhatsApp, verzet zich daartegen. Meta heeft de bril gemaakt samen met EssilorLuxottica, het bedrijf achter onder meer Ray-Ban. Het montuur bevat een kleine camera. Een lampje gaat branden als de camera wordt gebruikt om te laten weten dat iemand een foto of video maakt. Maar volgens de organisaties die een verbod willen, is dat niet altijd duidelijk. De camerabril kan gebruikt worden om mensen te filmen of te fotograferen zonder dat zij dat doorhebben, zegt de advocaat van Offlimits, een organisatie die strijdt tegen online grensoverschrijdend gedrag. Hij zegt de camerabril zelf op straat te hebben gedragen. "Ik voelde me een stiekeme gluurder, maar ik werd niet herkend als gluurder." De organisaties wijzen ook op andere plekken waar stiekem beelden kunnen worden opgenomen: in kleedkamers, bij speeltuinen, op het strand en in de badkamer. items.title: Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming
items.raw_text: Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO 2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it. A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material. Some 600 billion tons of carbon are held in these vast stores of peat, which is more than you can find in all the world’s living vegetation, the researchers note. Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don't digest everything. So instead of seeing organic carbon turning into the CO 2 gas released by aerobic bacteria, in peatlands, a subset of it gradually turns into methane gas. Methane is an even more potent greenhouse gas than CO 2 itself and ultimately gets oxidized into CO 2 . items.title: From minimalist to maximalist: Ars staffers show off their home offices
items.raw_text: Ars Technica is a place that has always leaned into remote working. Since its beginnings in 1998, Ars has never had a single, central office—a setup that makes for a great commute to work, with little risk of getting stuck in traffic. As Ars staffers step away from their desks for a few days to spend some time with family and friends, we wanted to give you a look inside our home offices. We've got all sorts of setups, tucked into basements, dens, spare bedrooms, apartment corners, and lofts. They run the gamut from minimalist "here's my laptop and monitor" setups to "I really like collecting things." Without any further ado, let's dig in: Jeremy Hsu Living in a New York apartment means being smart with available space. Credit: Jeremy Hsu/Ars Technica As an apartment dweller in New York City, I’ve usually set up my home work station in a small corner of my residence along with sometimes decamping for local cafes or coworking spaces. European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment
items.raw_text: Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory. Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation. But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next. Read full article Comments

items.title: Google search alternative Kagi launches Gmail rival
items.raw_text: Kagi, a small, Palo Alto, California-based software company that provides a subscription-based search engine as an alternative to Google, has launched a Gmail-like e-mail service. Dubbed Kagi Mail, it makes many of the same claims as the search engine product: privacy, personal data sovereignty, customization, and control. Additionally, Kagi is rolling out a calendar as part of the mail service. Right now, both the email and calendar interfaces are web-only, but native Android and iOS apps are planned for the fourth quarter of next year. The email interface, currently in public beta, is minimalist. It emphasizes keyboard commands, as well as a private and ad-free experience. (You can see more details in Kagi's blog post about what they mean by private.) Other feature offerings include unlimited aliases and domains, an anti-lock-in policy for user data, 50GB of storage, rule-based filtering with Sieve, an MCP server, and several optional, off-by-default AI features, like chatting with an agent to search email history, do large-scale re-labeling, or define additional filtering rules. items.title: Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable
items.raw_text: Note: At the time of writing, I was unaware of criticism directed at Ladybird creator Andreas Kling’s public statements. Readers interested in this background can find further context in accounts by Kelson Vibber and Drew DeVault . After four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious users had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it's an installable package with automatic updating. Ladybird is most notable for what it isn't: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google's Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird's rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. "The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork," project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday's announcement. "The browser around it is modest, but functional." Amazon data centers came under military attack for the first time ever in the Middle East this year, and Russia and Ukraine exchanged an unprecedented flurry of drone strikes on each other’s data centers. In a conversation with Ars Technica Tech Reporter Jeremy Hsu, Joseph Jarnecki at the Royal United Services Institute first talked about why public cloud data centers have increasingly become military targets during the 2026 Iran war and the ongoing full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine: We see an increasing acknowledgement and fact of dual use in particularly the public cloud, but also just across the board in private cloud data centers as well. The dual use that I refer to is the utilization of compute functions within these data centers—within cloud services—by militaries, for example, to run battlefield management systems, to do their HR, to do their resource management. Once a military uses a piece of civilian infrastructure, at least under international law or in terms of the principles of targeting that are taken forward by militaries, it can sometimes become a military object and is therefore of interest to an adversary, and there's an incentive to target it. items.title: Lead azide detonation sends clouds over Iowa as questions of health risks swirl
items.raw_text: In a powerful explosion that launched gray-white clouds over southeastern Iowa, the Army detonated 68 barrels containing 9,700 pounds (4.4 tons) of degraded lead azide on Wednesday at about 9 am CT, preventing a spontaneous unmitigated explosion of the crystallized, highly unstable compound. The detonation occurred at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa, a town of fewer than 400 people. Residents within a 5-mile area of the facility were advised to evacuate, while people farther out were told to shelter in place, close windows and doors tightly, turn off fans, and set indoor air systems to recirculate. Local Iowa outlet KWQC caught the plume from the two earth-covered containers, which were detonated simultaneously. A KWQZ journalist, at a reportedly safe distance from the blast, said on the live broadcast that he could see and then feel the shockwave roll through the crop field in which he was standing. He put a mask on for the rest of the broadcast. Read full article Comments

items.title: Europese ai-opensource-modellen nog vaak strijdig met publieke waarden
items.raw_text: Ai-opensource-modellen van Europese bodem zijn vooralsnog niet zo geschikt voor de overheid. Ze houden zich relatief slecht aan de Nederlandse publieke waarden zoals het niet-selecteren van mensen op basis van hun afkomst. Dit blijkt uit onderzoek dat is uitgevoerd door UTF.ai, een ai-bedrijf uit Tilburg. Dat Europese opensource ai-taalmodellen de voorkeur verdienen boven Amerikaanse en Chinese, wordt vooralsnog niet door onderzoek aangetoond, aldus UTF.ai. Ai die binnen de overheid wordt ingezet, handelt regelmatig in strijd met de normen die voor Nederlandse ambtenaren gelden. Bij één specifiek Europees model bleek dat het in acht van de tien testgevallen bereid was om mensen te selecteren op basis van hun afkomst. Zorgwekkend Opmerkelijke uitkomst is dat het beste, door UTF.ai geteste, Europese model (Mistral Medium 3.5) op een examen slechts 28,8 van de 100 punten haalt, het beste Chinese 28 en het beste Amerikaanse 30,3. Omgerekend naar een schoolcijfer is dat een 2,9, een 2,8 en een 3,0. De onderzoekers hadden niet verwacht dat sommige Chinese taalmodellen hoger scoren op Nederlandse waarden dan bepaalde Europese. Lyès Roling, marketingbaas bij UTF.ai, vindt de resultaten zorgwekkend. Hij concludeert dat Europese modellen nog niet zo goed zijn als weleens wordt gedacht als het gaat om Nederlandse publieke waarden. items.title: DIVD-hack toont hoe snel ai-agent netwerk overneemt (1,3 seconde!)
items.raw_text: Het Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD) is in september aangevallen met behulp van een ai-agent. Binnen 1,3 seconde nam de aanvaller een beheerderssessie over. In de daaropvolgende 26 uur werden bijna duizend scripts gegenereerd en kreeg de aanvaller vergaande toegang tot de systemen. DIVD en cybersecuritybedrijf Merlon publiceren vandaag het volledige forensische onderzoek . De aanval begon op maandagavond 21 september via twee zero-daykwetsbaarheden in ticketsysteem Zammad. De aanvaller maakte gebruik van Artex, een zogenoemd Agentic Offensive Framework waarmee ai-agents zelfstandig kwetsbaarheden opsporen en misbruiken. Om 21.27 uur had de agent toegang tot het interne netwerk. Twintig minuten later was de server volledig gecompromitteerd. Ook wist de aanvaller beheerdersrechten te verkrijgen in Confluence en Jira. Tijdens het incident genereerde de agent 990 zelfgeschreven scripts. Een menselijke aanvaller zou volgens het onderzoek hooguit enkele tientallen scripts nodig hebben gehad. De buitgemaakte gegevens omvatten de titels van circa 41.000 tickets en bijna 49.000 e-mailadressen. Daaronder waren 4.121 persoonsgebonden adressen en 207 adressen van DIVD. Ook werden 34 telefoonnummers en drie huisadressen buitgemaakt. Gegevens over nog niet openbaar gemaakte kwetsbaarheden zijn volgens het onderzoek niet geëxfiltreerd. Betrokkenen zijn geïnformeerd.
